intro: Styling hair builds service, judgment and client trust that many personal service jobs need. Of the 25 careers below, the closest by skills are retail sales and Opticians, Dispensing, both at a 72% match; opticians earn a BLS May 2025 median of $47,260, or 32% more than stylists earn.
why_it_works: A good stylist listens, suggests a look and keeps regular clients coming back. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.62 out of 5 for this job. The same client care runs through fitness instruction, eyewear fitting, floral design and massage. All 25 matches need no extra education. The skills to build are quality checking, running equipment, handling money and teaching others.
tips: Count your repeat clients and bookings; they prove you can build and keep a customer base.
Fitness instruction is a natural move: Exercise Trainers and Group Fitness Instructors earn $47,160, which is 32% more.
If you want your own business, learn bookkeeping, since managing money is one of your skill gaps.

faq.q: What jobs can former hairstylists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Retail Salespersons (72%), dispensing opticians (72%) and fitness trainers (71%), based on O*NET 31.0. Animal Trainers are also 71% matched, with a median of $39,990, which is 12% more than the $35,790 median for hairdressers, hairstylists and cosmetologists.

faq.q: Which careers for hairstylists pay more?
faq.a: 15 of the 25 matches pay more than styling hair. Athletes and Sports Competitors earn $66,710 (86% more), Embalmers $58,780 (64% more) and Massage Therapists $58,450 (63% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Spa Managers earn $69,770 for their broader group.

faq.q: Do cosmetologists need a degree to change careers?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than cosmetologists already have. In the closest match, 64% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, though some jobs, such as massage therapy and embalming, need a state license before you can work.

The skills that most often need work are quality control analysis, operation and control, managing financial resources and instructing. Judgment already rates 3.25 out of 5 for stylists in O*NET, so business and teaching skills are the next step for most moves.
